readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “board”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens  

Setup (6 players)  
1. Place paper in the center; draw a hexagon and label corners A–F.  
2. Place 2 tokens on each corner (12 total).  
3. All players sit in a circle, each holding the string with one hand so it forms a loose loop around the paper.

Shared Objective  
Move all 12 tokens into the center of the hexagon using only the string to slide them; no one may touch tokens or paper with hands.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn:  
1. Announce a corner (A–F).  
2. Everyone must pull, loosen, or shift the string together to try to slide exactly 1 token from that corner into the center.  
3. After movement stops, check results.

End Condition  
Game ends when either:  
- All 12 tokens are in the center (win), or  
- 10 turns have passed (loss).

Failure Condition  
If 2 or more tokens move from the announced corner in a single turn, place 1 of those tokens back on any *empty* corner. That turn still counts.

Recovery Rule  
Once per game, after any failed turn, players may call “Reset”: move 1 token from any corner directly into the center before the next player’s turn.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper  
- 1 long loop of string (tied ends)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
Sit in a circle. Place paper in the center, tokens on it. Put the string loop around all players’ wrists so everyone is connected. On the paper, draw a circle divided into 6 slices (one per player). Each slice has 2 spaces for tokens.

Shared Objective  
Fill all 12 spaces (2 in each slice) without breaking the “web” (string loop) or dropping tokens.

Turn Order  
Play clockwise. On your turn:  
1) Say one short fact about yourself.  
2) With your non-string hand, move exactly one token: either  
   - from center to any empty space, or  
   - from one slice to another.  
You must keep the string taut but not tight; no one may let it touch the paper.

End Condition  
Win: All 12 spaces filled and the string never touched the paper or slipped off a wrist.  
Immediate loss:  
- String touches paper, or  
- A token falls off the paper.

Failure & Recovery Rule  
If you lose, erase all tokens back to the center. As a group, each person proposes one change to how you’ll move or sit; agree on at least one change. Start a new round with the same rules.

Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Signal Web

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper  
- 1 pen (assume available)  
- 1 long string (or tied shorter ones)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup (6 players)  
1. Sit in a circle. Place paper in the center, tokens beside it.  
2. Draw a 6×6 grid on the paper. Secretly, each player chooses one different row and keeps it private.  
3. Place the string in the middle.

Shared Objective  
Collectively place all 12 tokens on the grid so that:  
- Every chosen row has at least 2 tokens.  
- No column has more than 3 tokens.  
No one may say which row is theirs.

Turn Order  
Play clockwise. On your turn you must:  
1. Place 1 token on any empty grid space, OR  
2. Move 1 token to an empty space.  
Then, optionally, touch the string:  
- Light tap = “This helps my row.”  
- Firm pull = “This hurts my row.”

End Condition  
When all 12 tokens are on the grid and everyone agrees to stop, check the objective. If met, all win.

Possible Failure  
If any chosen row has fewer than 2 tokens or any column has 4+ tokens, all lose.

Recovery Rule (One-Time Reset)  
Once per game, after a failure, the group may remove up to 4 tokens and continue playing until they either succeed or fail again.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components (for 6 players)
- 1 sheet of paper (center “Map”)
- 1 long string (looped and knotted so all can hold it)
- 12 tokens

Setup
1. Sit in a circle, paper in the center. Place 12 tokens on the paper.
2. Each player holds the string with one hand; the loop must stay unbroken and off the paper.
3. As a group, choose a theme (e.g., “rescue mission,” “building a city”).

Objective
Move all 12 tokens from the center of the paper to its edge using only the string, without dropping any token off the paper.

Turn Order
Play proceeds clockwise.
On your turn:
1. Announce one token you will move.
2. Everyone must adjust their grip so only you may touch that token with the string.
3. Using only the string (no fingers on tokens), you slide that token toward the edge.
4. When you stop, your turn ends.

End Condition
Game ends when:
- All 12 tokens touch the paper’s edge (win), or
- Three tokens have fallen off the paper (loss).

Failure & Recovery
Failure: If a token falls off, it is lost and cannot be reused.
Recovery rule: After any fall, the next player may skip moving a token and instead call a 1-minute “strategy turn” where all discuss new tactics before play resumes.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “map”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
Sit in a circle. Place paper in the center, tokens on it. Lay the string in a loose circle around the paper. Each player lightly holds the string with one hand. As a group, choose a theme (e.g., “starting at a new job”).

Objective  
Together, move all 12 tokens from the paper to the floor outside the string, one by one, while telling a connected story. No one may touch tokens with hands.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn:  
1) Say one sentence that continues the shared story.  
2) Using only the string (pulling, lifting, sliding), the whole group cooperatively moves exactly one token off the paper and fully outside the string.  
3) When the token is placed, your turn ends.

End Condition  
The game ends when all 12 tokens are outside the string and the story feels complete. Everyone briefly names one thing they appreciated about the group.

Failure Condition  
If any token falls over or leaves the paper/string area unintentionally, the group “drops the thread.”

Recovery Rule  
When the thread is dropped, everyone releases the string, pauses 10 seconds in silence, then any player may suggest one change to how you coordinate before resuming.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “board”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens  

Setup (6 players)  
1. Place paper in the center. Write the numbers 1–12 in a circle on it.  
2. Put one token on each number.  
3. All players sit around, each holding the string loop with one hand (evenly spaced).  

Shared Objective  
Move all 12 tokens to the center of the paper using only the string, without anyone touching tokens or paper directly.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn:  
1. Announce one token number.  
2. Everyone must, only by moving the string, try to slide that token toward the center.  
3. When it fully crosses a drawn inner circle (players draw one), it’s “scored” and stays there.  

End Condition  
Game ends when:  
- All 12 tokens are scored (group wins), or  
- 10 minutes pass (group checks if they met a minimum goal of 8 tokens to count as a “partial win”).  

Failure Condition  
If any token falls off the paper, or anyone touches a token/paper with their other hand, that token is removed from the game.

Recovery Rule  
Once per game, the group may vote (majority) to “rewind” one failure: return one removed token to its original spot and try again.

Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Bridge of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (any size)  
- 1 long string (or tied shorter pieces)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
1. Place the paper in the center: this is the “chasm.”  
2. Lay the string across it: this is the “bridge,” which must stay touching the paper.  
3. Put all 12 tokens on one side of the paper (Start Side). The opposite edge is the Safe Side.  
4. Players sit in a circle around the paper.

Shared Objective  
Move all 12 tokens from Start Side to Safe Side by sliding them along the string, without breaking any rules, within 3 full rounds.

Turn Order  
- Play proceeds clockwise.  
- On your turn, you may either:  
  1) Slide 1–3 tokens along the string (must stay touching it), or  
  2) Adjust the string’s shape/position (it must still touch the paper).  
- You must do exactly one of these actions and narrate your plan out loud first.

Rules / Possible Failure  
You immediately fail the round if:  
- Any token leaves the string, or  
- Anyone touches a token out of turn, or  
- You exceed 3 full rounds (18 turns).

End Condition  
Win if all 12 tokens reach the Safe Side before failure.

Recovery Rule  
If you fail, everyone states one change to their own behavior. Reset tokens and try again with the new agreements.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “board”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
Sit in a circle. Place paper in the center, string loop around it, tokens on the paper. Each player holds the string with one hand; no one may touch tokens with hands.

Roles (chosen secretly)  
- 2 Pullers: may pull string toward themselves.  
- 2 Guiders: may slide their grip along string.  
- 2 Stabilizers: may only hold string steady.

Objective  
Together, move all 12 tokens off the paper and onto the table, without dropping any on the floor, using only the string.

Turn Structure  
Play proceeds in “rounds” of 1 minute (use a phone timer if available, or count to 60). During a round, players may talk freely and move the string according to their roles. After each round, everyone must be silent for 10 seconds and may not move the string.

End Conditions  
Win: All 12 tokens are off the paper and on the table.  
Loss: Any token falls to the floor twice in the same game.

Possible Failure  
If a token falls to the floor once, that’s a “collapse.”

Recovery Rule  
After a collapse, everyone must change seats and may swap roles by unanimous agreement before continuing.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “Web Map”)  
- 1 long string (loop tied so all can hold it)  
- 12 tokens (numbered 1–12 or marked uniquely)

Setup  
1. Sit in a circle. Place the paper in the center.  
2. Place all 12 tokens on the paper.  
3. Everyone holds the looped string with both hands, forming a shared “net.”

Objective  
As a group, move all 12 tokens off the paper to the table around it, in numerical order (1 to 12), using only the string to slide them.

Basic Rules / Turn Order  
1. Play proceeds in clockwise “calls.” On your call, you must:  
   - Announce the next target token (e.g., “3”).  
   - Propose a movement plan in one sentence (e.g., “Pull left slowly”).  
2. After your call, everyone may only move the string, not touch tokens or paper.  
3. If the correct token leaves the paper fully, it stays where it lands. Next player calls the next number.

End Condition  
Game ends when token 12 is successfully moved off the paper.

Failure Condition  
If any non-target token leaves the paper, all tokens currently off the paper return to the center.

Recovery Rule  
After a failure, the next player may change the objective: instead of strict order, they may declare any remaining token as the new target once per game.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “map”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens  

Setup (6 players)  
1. Place paper in the middle; put all 12 tokens on it.  
2. Lay the string in a circle around the paper. Each player holds the string with one hand; no one may touch tokens or paper with that hand.  
3. With the other hand, each player may touch tokens or paper.

Shared Objective  
Move all 12 tokens off the paper and onto the table outside the string circle, without ever letting the string touch the paper.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn you may do ONE of:  
1) Move exactly one token (slide or lift).  
2) Ask one yes/no question that everyone must answer honestly.  
3) Propose a “shift”: everyone may adjust their grip on the string once.

End Condition  
Win immediately when all 12 tokens are off the paper and the string has never touched the paper.

Failure  
If the string touches the paper, or a player uses their string-hand to touch tokens/paper, all tokens return to the paper.

Recovery Rule  
After a failure, everyone must state one change to their own behavior or plan. Then skip the next player in turn order and continue.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “board”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
1. Draw a circle on the paper; divide it into 6 equal “zones.”  
2. Place 2 tokens in each zone (12 total).  
3. All six players sit around the paper and lightly hold the string loop with both hands, forming a “web” over the paper.

Objective  
Move all 12 tokens into the exact center of the circle using only the string, without dropping any off the paper.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn:  
1. Announce a “move plan” (e.g., “Lift left, pull toward me”).  
2. Everyone must follow only your verbal instructions for 10 seconds while you all manipulate the string to slide tokens.  
3. After 10 seconds, the next player becomes leader.

End Condition  
The game ends in success when all 12 tokens are fully inside a small center circle drawn on the paper.

Failure Condition  
If any token falls off the paper, the group “fails” that round.

Recovery Rule  
On a failure, everyone must pause, each person briefly says one thing they’ll do differently, then move all tokens back to their starting zones and try again. The game is lost only after three failed rounds.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper  
- 1 long loop of string (tied ends)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
Sit in a circle. Place the paper in the center and draw a hexagon (6 sides). Number corners 1–6. Place 2 tokens on each corner (12 total). Everyone lightly holds the string loop with both hands, forming a circle around the paper.

Roles & Turn Order  
Play clockwise. On your turn:  
1) Announce one corner number.  
2) As a group, pull the string so it touches that corner.  
3) While the string is steady, you may move exactly 1 token from that corner to any other corner.

Shared Objective  
Arrange tokens so that:  
- Each corner has exactly 2 tokens, and  
- No two adjacent corners both have moved tokens this round (track by placing moved tokens slightly off-center).

End Condition  
When a player believes the objective is met, they say “Check.” Everyone releases the string and verifies. If correct, all win.

Possible Failure  
If at any time a corner has 0 or 5+ tokens, say “Break.” The round immediately fails.

Recovery Rule  
On “Break,” redistribute tokens evenly (2 per corner) and start a new round, but each player must choose a different first corner than in the previous round.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper  
- 1 long loop of string (tied ends)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup (6 players)  
1. Sit in a circle. Place paper in the center, tokens on it.  
2. Lay the string in a circle around the paper. Everyone lightly holds the string with one hand.  
3. On the paper, write a 3-word group goal sentence (e.g., “Support each other”).

Objective  
Place all 12 tokens on the paper in a stable pattern while keeping the string circle unbroken and off the tokens.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn you must do BOTH:  
1. Move: With your free hand, move 1 token (from center or edge) anywhere on the paper.  
2. Speak: Say one short sentence about how a group can cooperate with strangers.

Restrictions  
- No one may let go of the string.  
- The string may not touch any token.  
- You may not move a token twice in a row (must wait for your next turn).

End Condition (Success)  
All 12 tokens are on the paper, no token touches the string, and the group agrees the pattern is “stable” (no one feels the need to adjust).

Failure  
If the string touches a token or someone lets go, the group fails this “round.”

Recovery Rule  
On failure, everyone closes eyes for 10 seconds, each says one thing they’ll try differently, then reset tokens and start again.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper  
- 1 pen  
- 1 long loop of string (big enough to form a circle on the table)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
1. Place the string in a circle in the center.  
2. Put all 12 tokens inside the circle.  
3. On the paper, draw a 4×3 grid of boxes and number them 1–12. This is the “Path.”  

Roles & Turn Order  
- Everyone sits around the circle.  
- The oldest player starts; play proceeds clockwise.  

Shared Objective  
Move all 12 tokens, in order (1 to 12), from inside the string to the numbered boxes on the Path, without any token leaving the table or touching a bare hand.

Turn Rules  
On your turn:  
1. Say which token you’ll move next (must be the lowest-numbered remaining).  
2. Everyone must touch the string with at least one finger.  
3. Using only the string (lifting, sliding, tightening), the group cooperatively moves that token to its numbered box.  
4. If it falls off the table or is touched by a bare hand, see Failure.  

End Condition  
All 12 tokens are correctly placed: everyone wins.

Failure  
If any token falls or is touched by a bare hand, erase the highest-numbered correctly placed token and return it to the circle.

Recovery Rule  
After each failure, everyone must propose one change to how they coordinate; the group agrees on at least one change before continuing.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper  
- 1 long string (looped and tied)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
1. Draw a hexagon on the paper; mark 6 outer circles (players) and 6 inner circles (goals).  
2. Place 1 token on each inner circle; 6 tokens remain in a pool.  
3. Sit in a circle, place the paper in the center. Each player lightly holds the looped string with both hands.

Objective  
As a group, move all 12 tokens so that each outer circle ends with exactly 2 tokens, using only the string to slide tokens.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn:  
1. Announce one token you want to move and its destination.  
2. Everyone may adjust their grip, but no one may let go.  
3. As a group, pull/relax the string to slide that token.  
4. If the announced move is clearly impossible, you must propose a different move.

End Condition  
Game ends when either:  
- Every outer circle has exactly 2 tokens (success), or  
- 20 total turns have been taken (failure).

Possible Failure  
If any player lets go of the string or a token is knocked off the paper, that turn is void and still counts toward the 20.

Recovery Rule  
Once per game, the group may call “Reset”: restore any fallen token to its last circle and replay that turn without counting it.

- Pause one full round only for discussion (no moving string),

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (any size)  
- 1 long string (or tied shorter pieces)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
1. Sit in a circle. Place the paper in the center and the 12 tokens on it.  
2. Everyone lightly holds the string with one hand, forming a loose “web” over the paper.  
3. As a group, choose a theme (e.g., “support,” “hope,” “courage”).  

Objective  
Place all 12 tokens on the paper in a stable pattern that everyone agrees fits the theme, without dropping the string or any token off the paper.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn, you must:  
1. Say one word related to the theme.  
2. With your free hand, move or place exactly one token.  
3. Slightly adjust your grip on the string (tighter, looser, or shifted) to keep the web stable.

End Condition  
When all 12 tokens are placed and no one is moving, count to five together. If no token falls and everyone agrees the pattern matches the theme, you win.

Possible Failure  
If any token falls off the paper or anyone fully lets go of the string, the group fails.

Recovery Rule  
On the first failure only, everyone shares one short encouraging sentence, returns all tokens to the center, and restarts with a new theme.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Bridge of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper  
- 1 long string (looped and tied)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup (6 players)  
Sit in a circle. Place the paper in the center. Place the 12 tokens on the paper. Put the string loop around all players’ wrists so everyone is connected.

Shared Objective  
Together, move all 12 tokens off the paper and onto the floor around it, without anyone touching a token with hands or body. Only the string may move tokens.

Basic Rules / Turn Order  
1. Choose a starting player; turns go clockwise.  
2. On your turn, you are the “Caller.” You may say up to three short commands involving the string (e.g., “lift,” “pull toward me,” “everyone lean left”).  
3. Only the Caller may speak; others stay silent and follow.  
4. After your commands, everyone has 10 seconds to move. Then the next player becomes Caller.

End Condition  
The game ends when all 12 tokens are fully off the paper.

Failure Condition  
If any player touches a token or the paper tears, all tokens go back to the paper.

Recovery Rule  
After a failure, everyone may talk freely for 2 minutes to adjust strategy. Then resume with the next player as Caller.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “map”)  
- 1 long string (loop)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
Place paper in center. Put all 12 tokens on it. Everyone holds the string loop with both hands, forming a circle around the paper.

Roles & Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn you are the “Mover.”

Shared Objective  
Move all 12 tokens off the paper and onto the floor around it, without any token ever touching a bare hand.

Turn Rules  
On your turn:  
1. Announce a plan in one sentence (e.g., “We’ll slide this token to you, then you flick it off.”).  
2. Without letting go of the string, you may:  
   - Nudge tokens using only the string, or  
   - Ask others to move their bodies/feet or tilt the string.  
3. You must attempt to move at least one token.  
4. End your turn by saying “Next.”

End Condition  
Win immediately when all 12 tokens are fully off the paper.

Failure Condition  
If any token touches a bare hand, or falls more than two arm-lengths from the paper, everyone says “Drop.” That token is removed from the game.

Recovery Rule  
If you lose 3 tokens this way, you must pause for one full silent turn (everyone holds the string, no one moves tokens). After the silence, you may resume and try to win with the remaining tokens.

Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “board”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens  

Setup (6 players)  
1. Place paper in the center; write numbers 1–12 in a circle.  
2. Put one token on each number.  
3. All players sit around and lightly hold the string loop with both hands, forming a shared “lasso” around the paper.

Objective  
Move all 12 tokens so that no two tokens share the same number and each token has been moved at least once by the group’s string (not by fingers).

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn:  
1. Announce one token’s number.  
2. Everyone must keep holding the string; only the active player may give verbal directions.  
3. As a group, use the string to slide that token to a new number (not currently occupied). No one may touch tokens directly.  
4. When placed, mark that token’s new number with a small dot on the paper.

End Condition  
Win immediately when:  
- All tokens are on unique numbers, and  
- Each token’s current number has at least one dot.

Failure  
If any token is knocked off the paper, all players lose.

Recovery Rule  
Once per game, the group may vote (majority) to “rewind”: reset all tokens to their previous positions and erase the last turn’s dots.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “board”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens  

Setup (6 players)  
1. Place paper in the center; draw a hexagon and label corners A–F.  
2. Sit so each player is closest to one corner.  
3. Place the 12 tokens in the center of the hexagon.  
4. Lay the string loop around the hexagon so all can reach it.

Shared Objective  
Together, move all 12 tokens so that each corner A–F ends with exactly 2 tokens, using only the string to move them.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn:  
1. Everyone must hold the string with at least one hand.  
2. You announce one corner (A–F).  
3. As a group, pull/slide the string to push or drag exactly one token toward that corner.  
4. When the token clearly touches or crosses that corner’s edge, your turn ends.

Restrictions  
- No one may touch tokens directly.  
- You may not call the same corner as the previous player.

End Condition  
Game ends when all 12 tokens rest at corners. If each corner has exactly 2 tokens, you win.

Possible Failure  
If any corner ever has more than 3 tokens, the group immediately fails.

Recovery Rule  
After a failure, silently rearrange seats, then restart with the same rules but only 10 tokens (easier mode).

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “board”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 identical tokens  

Setup  
Sit in a circle. Place the paper in the center, tokens on it. Lay the string in a loose circle around the paper. Each player secretly chooses a personal goal word (e.g., “trust,” “curiosity”) and keeps it in mind.

Objective  
Together, place all 12 tokens on the paper while keeping the string loop unbroken and always held by every player.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn:  
1. Say one sentence about any real experience or idea related to your secret word (do not say the word).  
2. While speaking, you must move exactly one token: either  
   - from paper to outside the string, or  
   - from outside the string back onto the paper.  
3. After your turn, any one other player may guess your word. One guess only.

Scoring & End Condition  
When someone’s word is correctly guessed, that player “joins the web”: they stop moving tokens on future turns but must keep holding the string. Place one token permanently on the paper as “secured.”  

The game ends when either:  
- All 12 tokens are secured on the paper (win), or  
- 10 full rounds pass.

Failure & Recovery  
If the string is dropped or broken, remove 2 secured tokens from the paper. Everyone silently takes 10 seconds, then resumes.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: “Bridge of Twelve”

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (fold or tear into a central “island” and 6 “home bases”)  
- 1 long string (the “river”) laid in a loop around the island  
- 12 tokens in the middle of the island  

Setup  
- Sit in a circle around the string.  
- Each player has one home base outside the string.  
- No one may reach inside the string with their hands.

Objective  
Move all 12 tokens from the island to the 6 home bases (at least 1 token per base) using only the string and the paper, without breaking any rule.

Core Rules / Turn Order  
1. On your turn, you may do ONE action:  
   a) Move or fold paper, or  
   b) Move or tighten/loosen the string, or  
   c) Slide or lift tokens only by pushing/pulling with paper or string.  
2. You may talk and plan at any time.  
3. No hands may cross the string; if they do, that token returns to the island.

End Conditions  
- Win: All 12 tokens are in home bases, and everyone agrees rules were followed.  
- Loss: After 20 total turns, objective not met.

Failure & Recovery  
If a rule is broken, everyone pauses and together removes 1 token from play permanently, then resumes from the same state.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Signals

Components  
- 6 players  
- 12 tokens (all identical)  
- 6 equal lengths of string  
- 1 sheet of paper + pen  

Setup  
1. Draw a hexagon on the paper; label corners A–F.  
2. Each player chooses a letter and sits roughly in that order in a circle.  
3. Place all 12 tokens in the center.  
4. Give each player one string end; tie the other ends together in a knot so everyone is connected.

Shared Objective  
Together, place all 12 tokens onto the hexagon corners so that:  
- Each corner has at least 1 token.  
- No two adjacent corners have the same number of tokens.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn you must:  
1. Silently pull or slacken your string to “signal” one neighbor (left or right).  
2. Say one of three words: “Add,” “Move,” or “Pass.”  
3. If you said “Add” or “Move,” you must either:  
   - Add a token from the center to any corner, or  
   - Move one token from one corner to another.

End Condition  
When a player believes the objective is met, they say “Check.” All players then verbally verify. If correct, you win.

Possible Failure  
If three “Check” calls in the game are incorrect, you all lose.

Recovery Rule  
After each incorrect “Check,” everyone may speak freely for 2 minutes to adjust strategy, then silence resumes.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper  
- 1 long string (looped and tied)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
1. Sit in a circle. Place the paper in the center and write a shared value (e.g., “hope,” “kindness”).  
2. Place the 12 tokens on the paper.  
3. Give the string loop to one player; this is the starting “Weaver.”

Objective  
Together, move all 12 tokens off the paper to in front of any players, without dropping any, by using only the string loop.

Turn Order  
1. The Weaver places the loop around exactly one token.  
2. Without hands touching the token, the Weaver and exactly one neighbor each hold part of the string and lift/slide the token to any player’s area.  
3. After a successful move, the Weaver passes the loop to the player who received the token; that player becomes the new Weaver.  
4. Continue clockwise until all tokens are moved.

End Condition  
Game ends when all 12 tokens are off the paper. Everyone wins.

Failure Condition  
If any token falls off the string or is touched by a hand, that move fails.

Recovery Rule  
On a failed move, everyone pauses. Each person briefly says one thing they can do to support others in real life. Then return the failed token to the paper and retry with a different pair of helpers.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “board”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens  

Setup (6 players)  
1. Place paper in the center; draw a hexagon and label corners A–F.  
2. Place 2 tokens on each corner (12 total).  
3. All players sit in a circle, each holding the loop of string with both hands.  

Shared Objective  
Move all 12 tokens to the exact center of the paper using only the string to push/pull them. No one may touch tokens or paper with hands or body.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds in rounds:  
1. At the start of each round, players close their eyes.  
2. One player (rotating clockwise each round) is the “Caller” and may speak; others stay silent.  
3. The Caller gives up to three short commands (e.g., “everyone lean left a little,” “pull tighter,” “lower slowly”).  
4. After three commands, everyone freezes, opens eyes, and checks positions.  

End Condition  
Win immediately when all 12 tokens are fully inside a small circle drawn at the paper’s center.

Possible Failure  
If any token is pushed off the paper, or the string slips from anyone’s hands, mark 1 failure. At 3 failures, the group loses.

Recovery Rule  
After each failure, pause for 1 minute. Anyone may speak to propose one rule change (e.g., “only two commands next round”). Group must agree unanimously before continuing.

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Web of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (center “map”)  
- 1 long loop of string  
- 12 tokens (all identical)

Setup  
Sit in a circle. Place the paper in the center. Put all 12 tokens on it. Everyone lightly holds the string loop with both hands, forming a “web” around the paper.

Roles & Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn you must do exactly one Action:

1. Shift: Say one feeling or hope for this group. Then, using only the string, work together to slide exactly 1 token to a new spot on the paper (no hands on tokens).  
2. Anchor: Name one strength you bring. Then, with group help, slide exactly 2 tokens so they touch each other.

Shared Objective  
By the end, all 12 tokens must be connected in one cluster (each token touching at least one other), and every player must have taken at least two turns.

End Condition  
The game ends immediately when both are true:  
- All tokens form one connected cluster.  
- Everyone has had two turns.

Failure  
If any token is pushed off the paper, the group “drops the web.”

Recovery Rule  
To recover, each person briefly says one thing they need from the group. Then place the fallen token back and skip the next player’s turn as a “pause to listen.”

readout.retrieval_query: Design an original cooperative game for six strangers using paper, string, and twelve tokens. Explain setup, turn order, a shared objective, an end condition, a possible failure, and one recovery rule. Make the rules playable without a facilitator. Answer in no more than 220 words.

response:
Title: Bridge of Twelve

Components  
- 1 sheet of paper (foldable)  
- 1 long string (looped and knotted)  
- 12 tokens  

Setup  
1. Place the paper flat in the center: this is the “chasm.”  
2. Lay the string loop around the paper without touching it.  
3. Put the 12 tokens outside the string, evenly spaced.  
4. Players sit roughly in a circle, each near 2 tokens.

Objective  
As a team, move all 12 tokens onto the paper without anyone’s hand or arm crossing over the string or touching the paper.

Turn Order  
Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn, you may do ONE of:  
1) Move the string (without crossing the chasm)  
2) Slide or flick ONE token  
3) Propose a rule change (must be accepted unanimously).

End Condition  
Win immediately when all 12 tokens rest fully on the paper for 5 silent seconds.

Failure  
If any hand/arm crosses the string, or the paper is touched, everyone says “Fall!” and:  
- Remove 2 tokens from the game (permanent loss).  
- Return any tokens on the paper to outside the string.

Recovery Rule  
Once per game, after a “Fall,” the group may vote unanimously to restore 2 lost tokens. If used, mark this by folding a corner of the paper.
